property_summary: For any caller, after a successful Put(...) the caller's recorded balance in C increases by the exact msg.value (i.e., Acc[caller].balance == previous + msg.value); the mutated modifier inverts the lock allowing reentrant behavior that can cause the recorded balance to not reflect the sent value for some inputs (reentrant attacker), breaking this invariant.

For any caller and any sent value, after calling Put the contract's Acc[caller].balance must be >= the sent msg.value (i.e., Put always records at least the deposited amount); the mutated modifier inverts the lock allowing a reentrant attacker to withdraw/modify state during Put and can make Acc[attacker].balance less than the sent value for some inputs, violating the rule.

For any depositor and deposit amount, after a single external Put(...) call from that depositor the contract's recorded Acc[depositor].unlockTime is at least the block.timestamp at the time of the call (Put sets unlockTime = max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)); the mutated modifier's inverted lock allows a reentrant attacker to call back into Put and arrange for Acc[attacker].unlockTime to be less than block.timestamp for some inputs, violating this invariant.

For any depositor and deposit amount, after a single Put(...) call the recorded Acc[depositor].balance is equal to the total value the depositor has sent (i.e., the deposit is recorded atomically and cannot be reduced via reentrancy during Put); the inverted-lock mutant allows a reentrant attacker to withdraw during Put and make Acc[attacker].balance smaller than the value sent, violating this invariant for some inputs.

For any depositor address and deposit amount, after calling Put(amount) the contract's recorded Acc[depositor].balance is at least the contract's own balance that owes that depositor (i.e., address(c).balance >= Acc[depositor].balance) — the inverted-lock mutant allows a reentrant attacker to withdraw during Put so that the contract's recorded per-user balance can exceed the contract's actual ETH holdings for that user, violating the relation for some inputs.

Invariant: After calling Put(x) from any externally owned account with value >= MinSum, the caller's recorded balance in c.Acc equals the sent value (no unexpected extra deductions); removing the non-reentrancy guard allows a reentrant attacker during Put to change the stored balance so this can be violated.

For any caller, after a single external Put call that sends some ETH, the caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance equals the amount sent (Put is atomic and cannot be altered by reentrancy); removing the nonReentrant require allows a reentrant attacker to cause the stored balance to differ.

For any attacker-controlled caller that performs Put(value) (value >= MinSum) via an external contract which reenters in receive(), the reference contract ensures the caller's recorded Acc[caller].balance equals the total ETH sent after Put returns (reentrancy blocked); the mutant without the require allows reentrant Collect during Put and can make Acc[attacker].balance smaller than the ETH sent.

For any caller and any sent value, after calling Put(...) the contract's public mapping Acc records a non-decreasing balance for that caller (i.e., Acc[caller].balance >= previous balance) — removing the nonReentrant require allows reentrant calls during Put that can *decrease* the caller's recorded balance during the single Put call.

For any caller and any sent value, a call to Put(...) always increases that caller's stored Acc[msg.sender].balance by exactly msg.value (i.e., after Put returns, Acc[caller].balance == old + msg.value); removing the require in the nonReentrant_ modifier enables reentrant Collect during Put which can reduce the recorded balance and violate this rule for some inputs.

After any successful Put(from, value, unlockTime) call, the stored Acc[from].unlockTime is at least the call's block.timestamp in the reference (it equals max(inputUnlockTime, block.timestamp)), whereas the mutant overwrites it to block.timestamp unconditionally and thus can make it smaller than the intended input unlockTime when inputUnlockTime > block.timestamp.

For any caller, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the stored Acc[caller].unlockTime is at least block.timestamp and if the provided _unlockTime is strictly greater than block.timestamp then the stored unlockTime equals that provided value (the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp can make the stored unlockTime smaller than the supplied _unlockTime).

For any caller and any _unlockTime, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the stored Acc[caller].unlockTime is never less than block.timestamp and, furthermore, if the supplied _unlockTime is strictly greater than block.timestamp then Acc[caller].unlockTime equals the supplied _unlockTime; the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp can make Acc[caller].unlockTime smaller than the supplied _unlockTime when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

For any caller and any _unlockTime, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the stored Acc[caller].unlockTime is >= block.timestamp and equals _unlockTime whenever _unlockTime > block.timestamp; the mutant that unconditionally sets unlockTime = block.timestamp can make Acc[caller].unlockTime smaller than the supplied _unlockTime (violating the equality case).

For any caller and any supplied _unlockTime, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the stored Acc[caller].unlockTime is >= block.timestamp and, if _unlockTime > block.timestamp, equals _unlockTime; the mutant that always writes block.timestamp can make Acc[caller].unlockTime smaller than the supplied _unlockTime (violating the equality when _unlockTime > block.timestamp).

For any caller and any provided _unlockTime and deposit value, the reference contract always sets the caller's stored unlockTime to at least the current block.timestamp (i.e. acc.unlockTime >= block.timestamp after Put); the mutant can set acc.unlockTime to a past timestamp allowing acc.unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs, breaking this invariant.

For every call to Put by any address with any _unlockTime and any payable value, the reference always ensures the stored unlockTime for that caller is >= block.timestamp (it never sets a past unlockTime); the mutant can set a past unlockTime, breaking this invariant.

For any caller, after Put completes the reference contract ensures the caller's stored unlockTime is never less than the current block.timestamp (it sets unlockTime = max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)); the mutant that assigns unlockTime = _unlockTime can make stored unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs, violating this invariant.

For every call to Put(msg.sender, _unlockTime, value) the reference ensures Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it takes the max of _unlockTime and block.timestamp); the mutant that assigns unlockTime = _unlockTime can produce Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime, violating this invariant.

For any address and any _unlockTime and deposit value, after calling Put the reference contract guarantees Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp OR acc.balance == 0 (i.e., if a deposit was made, unlockTime is not in the past); the mutant can set unlockTime to a past timestamp while having a positive balance, violating this rule.

For any caller and any payable amount, after calling Put(...) the caller's Acc[msg.sender].balance increases by exactly the sent msg.value (i.e., address's stored balance increments by msg.value); the mutant removed the update so this rule can be violated when msg.value>0.

For any caller and any nonzero sent value, after calling Put(...) the contract's Acc[caller].balance is at least the sent msg.value (i.e., calling Put increases the stored balance by the sent amount); the mutant removed the balance update so for some inputs (msg.value>0) the stored balance does not reflect the sent value.

For any caller and any nonzero msg.value, after calling Put(...) the contract's balance (address(c).balance) increases by exactly the sent msg.value (the reference forwards received ETH into contract storage by the payable call); the mutant still accepts ETH but does not update its internal Acc mapping, so there exists inputs where the public Acc[msg.sender].balance does not reflect the sent msg.value — we instead assert about address(c).balance change which the reference preserves but the mutant also preserves, so to catch the mutant we assert that Acc[msg].balance equals address(c).balance when only a single actor ever deposits (the mutant breaks this because it fails to record the deposit).

For any depositor and any deposit amount, if that depositor is the only account that has ever sent ETH to the contract, then the contract's public Acc[depositor].balance equals address(c).balance (the reference records deposits in its mapping; the mutant fails to update the mapping and thus can break this equality for some inputs).

For any depositor and any nonzero deposit amount when that depositor is the only account that has ever sent ETH to the contract and calls Put with any unlockTime, the contract's public Acc[depositor].balance equals the total ETH held by the contract (address(c).balance); the mutant that removes the line updating Acc[...] can accept ETH but will break this equality for some deposit amounts (>0).

For any caller, Collect may only succeed when block.timestamp is strictly greater than the caller's stored unlockTime (i.e., Collect is blocked at unlockTime); the mutant that changes the check to >= allows Collect to succeed at block.timestamp == unlockTime and thus can withdraw one block earlier.

For any caller and any amounts, the reference contract C only allows Collect to succeed when block.timestamp > stored unlockTime (i.e., it must be strictly greater); the mutant allowing >= can let Collect succeed when block.timestamp == unlockTime, so there exists an input (timestamp equal to unlockTime) where mutant permits success but reference does not.

For every admissible input, the reference C always rejects a Collect call made exactly at block.timestamp == stored unlockTime (i.e., Collect only succeeds when block.timestamp > unlockTime); the mutant changes the check to >= allowing Collect to succeed when block.timestamp == unlockTime, so there exists inputs (unlockTime == current timestamp) where mutant permits withdrawal but reference does not.

For any caller and amounts, the reference contract C never allows Collect to succeed at a block.timestamp equal to the stored unlockTime (it requires strictly greater); the mutant that changes the check to >= can allow Collect to succeed when block.timestamp == unlockTime, so there exists an admissible input (timestamp == unlockTime with sufficient balance) where the mutant permits withdrawal but the reference rejects it.

For all inputs, the reference contract C only allows Collect to succeed when block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime (strictly greater); the mutant changes this to >= allowing a Collect to succeed when block.timestamp == acc.unlockTime, so there exist inputs (caller, amount, timestamp equal to stored unlockTime with sufficient balance) where mutant permits withdrawal but reference does not.

For any caller and amount, Collect never allows withdrawing an amount when the caller's balance is below MinSum (1 ether); the mutant removing that check permits withdrawals for balances < MinSum for some inputs.

For any caller and amount, if a caller's balance before Collect is less than MinSum (1 ether) then Collect must NOT successfully send funds out (i.e., the call must fail or not transfer) — the mutant removes the MinSum check allowing successful Collect for small balances in some cases.

For any caller and amount, if the caller's stored balance before Collect is strictly less than MinSum then Collect() must not transfer any Ether out (i.e., address(c).balance remains == sum of deposits) — the mutant removing the MinSum check allows a successful withdrawal for some small-balance inputs, violating this rule.

For any caller and amount, if the caller's stored balance before Collect is less than MinSum (1 ether), then calling Collect(...) MUST NOT successfully transfer Ether out (i.e., the external call from Collect must fail or not be made); the mutant removing the acc.balance>=MinSum check allows Collect to succeed for some small balances, violating this rule.

For every caller, if their stored acc.balance is less than MinSum then calling Collect(...) must NOT result in a successful external transfer (the call out must fail or not be executed); the mutant that removes the acc.balance>=MinSum check allows a successful withdrawal for some small balances, violating this.

Invariant: after a successful Collect call the holder's recorded balance decreases by exactly the collected amount (i.e., balance_after = balance_before - amount) — the mutant removing the nonReentrant lock allows a reentrant attacker to drain extra funds, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and amounts, a single call to Collect cannot be reentered to withdraw more than the caller's recorded balance (i.e., after Collect returns the holder's stored balance is >= 0 and never decreased below zero by reentrancy); removing the nonReentrant_ assignment enables a reentrant attacker to drain extra funds causing the post-call stored balance to be lower than it should be.

For any holder and amounts, a single call to Collect that transfers _am and returns normally preserves that holder's recorded balance decreased by exactly _am (i.e., Acc[attacker].balance after == before - _am); removing the locked_ = true allows a reentrant attacker to withdraw more than _am, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and amounts where Collect succeeds, after Collect returns the caller's recorded balance is strictly less than or equal to its pre-call balance and never increases due to reentrancy; removing the locked_ = true allows a reentrant attacker to call back during Collect and cause the stored balance to end up lower than expected for some inputs (violating the monotonic non-increase rule), which the test detects by deploying an attacker that reenters Collect.

For any caller, after a single Collect call that returns successfully the contract's recorded balance for that caller has decreased by exactly the requested amount; removing the locked_ = true lets a reentrant attacker withdraw more than requested so this equality can be violated for some inputs.
